images.title: Floors under the ground
images.purpose: Show that a building has 5 floors under the thick ground line and the Welcome Hall on the ground line itself.
images.composition: One tall building centred, drawn as a column of equal floor rows, with a thick ground line across it and a short label on the right.
images.exact_structure: One column of 7 equal floor rows, all the same width. The top row has a plain outline. Row 2 sits on a thick grey #6B7280 ground line and is filled reddish purple #CC79A7. Rows 3 to 7, which are 5 rows below the ground line, are filled amber #E69F00. Exactly 1 building, 7 rows, 1 ground line, 1 purple ground floor row, 5 amber rows.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any extra floor, dot, arrow or row beyond the counts stated
unequal floor rows or unequal arrow lengths
images.takeaway: Some floors are below the ground, and the ground floor sits on the line.
images.description: A column of 7 equal floor rows: a plain top row, a purple ground floor row on a thick grey line, and 5 amber rows below it.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the amber floors below the line and name the floor that sits on the line.

image_decisions.why: Counting floors on both sides of the ground line is a picture idea; one clean image carries it.
